recommendedOrder: Inspect the six SECURITY DEFINER functions' bodies, search_path, candidate ownership checks, argument validation and EXECUTE grants. Do not revoke/alter until callers and intended backend-only functions are mapped.

Classify all 17 RLS-enabled/no-policy tables as backend-only or missing-policy. For backend-only tables prove client roles cannot access them and service-role access remains constrained by server policy/audit.
Review all 16 multiple-permissive-policy findings, especially roles with multiple broad policies on candidate_credentials and candidate_sessions.
Enable and verify Supabase leaked-password protection in a planned auth configuration change after review.
Do not drop the 282 unused-index candidates automatically; measure representative workload and preserve indexes used for foreign keys, rare paths or future launches.

liveDatabaseVerification.disposition: The 6 SECURITY DEFINER advisor findings are not, by themselves, evidence of an anonymous exposure. Live ACL checks show PUBLIC and anon cannot execute them, and each deployed function body matches the reviewed historical source candidate after whitespace normalization. Authenticated execution remains allowed and requires role-specific negative E2E tests. All 17 RLS/no-policy tables deny direct anon/authenticated table privileges and are candidates for intentional backend-only classification, not for broad policy creation.
